chunk_text: Pillai College of Engineering follows the curriculum provided by the University of Mumbai. The curriculum planning and delivery are diligent with the preparation of the lesson plan, adapting Bloom's Taxonomy focusing on Information, Understanding, Application, and Synthesis. Academic calendar is prepared and lesson plans are reviewed by HODs. Teachers maintain course files documenting all details of lectures, attendance, and internal marks. Project-based learning (PBL) is institutionalized from the first year onwards.

The curriculum at Pillai College of Engineering integrates cross-cutting issues like professional ethics, gender equality, human values, and environmental sustainability. Mandatory courses in Business Communication & Ethics, Cyber Security, and Intellectual Property Rights are embedded. The Nature Club organizes annual cleanliness drives (including the Gadhi River cleaning project), tree plantation drives, and carbon-neutral campus awareness campaigns.

PCE assesses the learning levels of students after admission through diagnostic tests and continuous internal assessments. Slow learners are identified based on their performance in first internal tests and are supported via scheduled remedial classes, specialized study camps, and bilingual tutorial sessions. Advanced learners are encouraged to participate in national hackathons (Smart India Hackathon), publish research papers, and attend guidance classes for competitive examinations such as GATE, GRE, and CAT.
section_heading: Catering to Student Diversity (Slow vs Advanced Learners)

chunk_text: PCE has a dedicated mentor-mentee scheme where a small group of students (approx 15-20) is allotted to a faculty mentor. Mentors hold fortnightly meetings to discuss academic progress, personal grievances, and career aspirations. Mentoring registers track attendance, psychological well-being, and academic performance. Professional counselors are also available on campus for confidential psychological counseling.

PCE utilizes student-centric methods like project-based learning (PBL) from the first year itself. Every semester, students complete projects crossing multiple subjects. The college has an advanced Maker Studio equipped with 3D printers, laser cutters, PCB milling, and CNC machines for rapid prototyping. Students also access an on-campus Component Library to borrow electronic sensors, microcontrollers, and actuators for academic and innovative projects.

The Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) established in 2017 conducts annual Academic and Administrative Audits (AAA) to review teaching-learning processes and institutional governance. The IQAC pioneered project-based learning and established the Component Library. The Academic Monitoring System (AMS) tracks attendance, daily lecture entries, and syllabus coverage dynamically across all academic programs.
